title: A young convert is called to cry repentance before Christ comes
setting: Orson Pratt was baptized by his older brother Parley on 19 September 1830, his nineteenth birthday. In October he traveled more than 200 miles to Fayette, New York, where Joseph Smith was staying. He asked Joseph to inquire of the Lord about his duty. Joseph dictated this revelation on 4 November 1830 in Orson’s presence, and John Whitmer wrote it down. Orson was ordained an elder about a month later and began preaching in Colesville.
summary: The voice in the revelation speaks as Jesus Christ, the light of the world. It recalls that he gave his life so believers might become God’s sons. On that basis it calls Orson his son. Orson is blessed for believing and more blessed for being called to preach. He is told to cry repentance loudly to a “crooked and perverse generation”. The revelation describes signs before Christ’s coming: a darkened sun, a blood-red moon, and falling stars. It tells Orson to prophesy by the Holy Ghost and promises to be with him if he is faithful.

contextNote.title: Why Orson is called a son
contextNote.text: Orson Pratt was new to the faith and only nineteen. Verse 1 opens with “My son Orson”, and verse 3 explains the title. It says Christ gave his life so believers “might become the sons of God”. Verse 4 adds that Orson is blessed because he has believed. So sonship here rests on belief in Christ’s sacrifice, not on age or experience. Verse 5 then builds on that standing with a call to preach. In this passage, being a son is the ground from which the mission grows.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 30–36 calls readers to lift up their voices and witness of Jesus Christ. Verses 3–5 move from Christ’s sacrifice to Orson’s sonship to his call to preach; how does that order shape your view of service?
reviewNote: Read all 12 verses. Official heading gives Fayette, 4 November 1830, Orson Pratt age nineteen, baptized about six weeks earlier after Parley’s preaching. JSP introduction supplied the October trip, his request, John Whitmer as scribe, and the 1 December ordination; JSP notes Pratt later named Colesville as his mission field, though the text names no place. Fact-check 2026-10-12: contextNote now attributes the claim about Christ’s sacrifice to verse 3 (historical voice). Setting confirmed against JSP.
